<description>
`mining_prioritisetransaction.py` checks that `prioritisetransaction` alone makes `getblocktemplate` return a new block, by comparing the whole template before and after moving mocktime 10 seconds forward. But `curtime` comes from the clock, so the two templates always differ, even if the template wasn't rebuilt.

This PR checks that the deprioritised transaction drops out of the template instead.
If you remove the counter bump in `CTxMemPool::PrioritiseTransaction` (the fix this check was added for in #10196), the test from master still passes but this one fails.
</description>

Confirmed that the check on master cannot fail because `curtime` is refreshed on every `getblocktemplate` call. So the `setmocktime(mock_time+10)` bump makes the two templates not the same whether or not a rebuild happened.

Tested this out by commenting out `++nTransactionsUpdated` in `CTxMemPool::PrioritiseTransaction` and rebuilding it. And so on master, `assert_not_equal(template, new_template)` still passes, but with this PR, `assert tx_id not in template_txids()` fails. But the PR test passes again once the line is restored.
